response_content: {"selected_paradigms": ["clique_density", "attr_struct_mismatch", "community", "subgraph_contrast"], "rationale": "clique_density shows the most separated landmarker tail (mean 0.035, p50 0.010, p99 0.550 -> ~5 std jump), and the profile's moderate clustering_coeff (0.231) combined with very high modularity (0.785) supports real dense-subgraph/collusion structure for closure-weighted triangle participation to catch. attr_struct_mismatch has the second-strongest tail (mean 0.064, p99 0.397, ~4 std) and is well-grounded by the extreme feature richness/sparsity (feature_dim=8337, sparsity=0.9965) paired with clear structure, giving cross-modal rank divergence real signal to exploit that pure structural or pure attribute views would miss. community is directly supported by the profile itself (modularity=0.7849 across 52 communities is a strong, well-formed partition) and its landmarker tail (mean 0.382, p99 0.708, ~2.9 std) confirms a subpopulation of nodes poorly explained by any community, complementing the clique-level structural view with a global-adherence view. subgraph_contrast is included as the local/contextual complement: its cheap-probe tail (mean 0.491, p99 0.793, ~2.3 std) is explicitly noted as an underestimate of the full-run signal, and it is designed to fuse with clique_density to jointly cover contextual (RWR-subgraph) and structural (clique) anomaly populations.
